concerns.text: The power‑analysis (T013b) simulates required n for macro‑F1 ≥ 0.70, power ≥ 0.8, yet the pipeline proceeds with training even when n < 150 (using leave‑one‑out). With such small samples the macro‑F1 estimate is highly unstable, so the study is likely under‑powered to meet SC‑001; a more rigorous sample‑size justification or a minimum‑size cutoff is needed.

FR‑001 permits rule‑based synthetic labeling, but FR‑008 mandates exclusion of records without a curated label and aborts if *all* records lack one. This contradictory handling of missing labels creates a risk that the training set will be empty or dominated by synthetic labels, undermining construct validity of the ‘degradation pathway’ target.

A χ² test is applied to motif‑importance frequencies derived from Integrated Gradients scores. χ² assumes independent categorical counts and sufficient expected cell frequencies; IG scores are continuous and correlated across motifs, violating test assumptions and threatening statistical validity of SC‑002.

Environmental variables (temperature, pH, UV) are imputed with fixed defaults and treated as global graph attributes. No explicit strategy is described to control for confounding introduced by imputation, and the sensitivity analysis (T018a) only compares three imputation strategies without assessing whether the imputed values drive the learned associations, risking biased attributions (SC‑005).
